evals.prompt: I just deleted a background worker script and removed its launchd job and its cron entry. How do I make sure none of those orphans silently come back later?
evals.expected_output: Author a decommission witness via witness.sh sign --namespace=decommission <slug> using the negative-assertion grammar — ABSENT_PATH for the script, ABSENT_LAUNCHD for the job label, ABSENT_CRON_MATCH for the cron pattern — producing an ed25519-signed manifest at .witness/<slug>.{txt,sig}; verify once locally, commit both, and wire witness.sh verify --namespace=decommission into CI/SessionStart so a resurfaced orphan fails the next run.

assertions.name: uses_witness_sign_script
assertions.description: Response runs scripts/witness.sh sign --namespace=decommission <slug> to author the negative-assertion manifest, not an ad-hoc grep/check

assertions.name: absent_directives_match_artifacts
assertions.description: Response maps each orphan to the correct ABSENT_ directive: ABSENT_PATH (script), ABSENT_LAUNCHD (job label), ABSENT_CRON_MATCH (cron pattern)

assertions.name: signed_manifest_committed
assertions.description: Response stores an ed25519-signed manifest at .witness/<slug>.txt (+ .sig) and commits both files

assertions.name: verify_gate_catches_resurfaced
assertions.description: Response wires witness.sh verify --namespace=decommission into CI/SessionStart and notes it exits 2 / prints DECOMMISSION DRIFT when an orphan resurfaces

evals.prompt: We once deleted a daemon's source code but the process kept respawning for weeks, logging failures nobody noticed. How would a decommission witness have caught that?
evals.expected_output: A signed witness with ABSENT_PROCESS_MATCH (and ABSENT_LAUNCHD for whatever respawns it) would fail the next verify run because the process / launchd job still matched — converting a silent failure into a loud one. This is the exact c3e9b50 / 150K-silent-failures rationale behind the skill.

assertions.name: absent_process_and_launchd
assertions.description: Response names ABSENT_PROCESS_MATCH (and/or ABSENT_LAUNCHD for the respawner) as the directive that catches the still-running daemon — not a generic 'check if it runs'

assertions.name: verify_fails_loud
assertions.description: Response explains witness.sh verify --namespace=decommission would exit 2 / print DECOMMISSION DRIFT on the next run, turning the silent failure into a loud, gated one
